subtitle: Manage application demand across wires, compute, and storage.
summary: Pip’s film travels through more than wires. Origin servers, caches, access networks, and viewers’ devices all do work. Compression and caching can reduce transfers while adding compute or storage, so Pip follows the whole delivery path. Changing global internet routing is not a quick local fix; applications can reduce unnecessary traffic and use established delivery controls. The book’s pandemic examples show preparation ahead of demand and lighter optional quality. Pip borrows that flexibility without assuming a cache or a smaller download is automatically carbon aware.

concepts.title: The internet includes more than wires
concepts.body: Pip follows a film from the origin to a viewer: backbone, metro, and last-mile links carry it through independently operated networks. Caches, compression, compute, and storage help along the way. Counting downloaded bytes alone misses much of the system. Even a satellite connection brings access benefits, equipment lifetime, infrastructure, and wider consequences. Pip draws the whole delivery path before deciding which resource to change.

steps.text: Pip follows the entire delivery boundary.
The origin stores and processes the film.
The viewer’s device also consumes resources.

concepts.title: Compression trades one resource for another
concepts.body: “Make the file smaller,” says Pip, reaching for the encoder again. But this video is already compressed. Extra encoding and decoding could consume more work for little transfer reduction. Pip compares actual compressibility, processor costs, network conditions, and hardware support across the full delivery path. A smaller payload is useful evidence about bytes—not proof of lower carbon. The chosen rendition must still meet the viewer’s need.

steps.text: Pip asks whether another compression pass is worthwhile.
Include decoding and the viewer’s required quality.

concepts.title: Application decisions are a practical lever
concepts.body: Pip sees a long network route and imagines rewriting the internet’s directions. Those directions cross autonomous systems and reflect commercial relationships and routing policy; the book warns that carbon-aware changes to BGP are complex and risky. Pip controls the cinema app more directly. Conditional updates can replace repeated full downloads, and established delivery controls can reduce unnecessary traffic. Moving application work is different from changing public-internet routing.

steps.text: Pip distinguishes two different intervention points.
Public routing spans autonomous systems and commercial policy.
Send required changes instead of repeatedly downloading everything.

concepts.title: Caching can shift work ahead of demand
concepts.body: The premiere crowd has not arrived, but Pip can place likely popular film versions in nearby caches. Preparation happens before demand while viewers still choose when to watch. That flexibility reduces repeated long-distance transfers, yet stored copies and unused prefetches cost resources. Pip measures which copies actually serve viewers. A CDN creates room to shift work; it needs an electricity signal influencing that work before Pip can call it carbon aware.

steps.text: Pip predicts a popular release, with uncertainty.
Prepare selected renditions before requests arrive.
Viewers keep their chosen watching time; unused copies still count.

concepts.title: Graceful degradation preserves essentials
concepts.body: A visitor’s connection falters. Pip lowers optional video detail while keeping clear audio and captions. Graceful degradation preserves the essential experience under constraint, as the book’s pandemic examples illustrate. The controls must already be designed and understood. To use this flexibility for electricity, Pip needs a relevant carbon or power signal and an agreed minimum service. Randomly making the picture worse does not establish a sustainability benefit.

steps.text: A relevant resource or electricity signal informs the response.
Keep the audio, captions, and functionality users need.

misconceptions.claim: Compressing every payload always saves energy.
misconceptions.correction: Compression adds compute; evaluate actual size reduction and encoding and decoding costs.

misconceptions.claim: A CDN is automatically carbon aware.
misconceptions.correction: Caching provides shifting capability. Carbon awareness additionally requires an electricity signal that influences operation.

scenario.title: Prepare a popular video release
scenario.context: Pip expects a crowd for a new film. Popular renditions could wait in regional caches or be transformed on demand. Small screens and large displays need different versions. The popularity forecast may be wrong; preparing every format everywhere could leave unused copies and wasted work.

options.label: Precompute and stage likely renditions
options.benefit: Reduces repeated origin work and smooths the peak transfer load.
options.cost: Uses storage and preparation that may be wasted if demand differs from the forecast.
options.consequence: The service places likely popular versions and measures cache use. It keeps less common formats on demand until their demand justifies staging.

options.label: Generate and transfer on demand
options.benefit: Avoids speculative renditions that nobody requests.
options.cost: Concentrates processing at request time and may repeat work during a surge.
options.consequence: The team measures latency and repeated conversions, then considers selective caching where observed reuse supports the extra stored copy.

scenario.debrief: Demand predictability and reuse determine the best balance. A bandwidth improvement is evidence about delivery, not by itself a complete carbon result.

quiz.question: A cached video was prepared earlier but served when requested. What was shifted?
quiz.explanation: Preparation and transfer can be decoupled from demand while the user still watches at the chosen time.

quiz.question: Why assess compression beyond bytes saved?
options: Encoding and decoding also consume resources
quiz.explanation: The complete path includes compute as well as transmission.

quiz.question: What does the chapter favor as an initial networking intervention?
options: Reduce unnecessary application traffic and use established delivery controls
Assume lower-layer efficiency removes every opportunity
quiz.explanation: The authors identify application behavior as a more accessible and controllable source of improvements.

exercise.title: Design a delivery strategy
exercise.prompt: Select a large or frequently requested asset. Compare immediate generation with selective preprocessing and caching, then define an essential service mode.
